title: The fibres of an etale morphism are disjoint unions of spectra of finite separable field extensions
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $s\in S$ with residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre [def-pc-base-change]. Then $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(s)$: the underlying topological space of $X_s$ is discrete (every point of $X_s$ is open and closed in $X_s$), and for every point $y\in X_s$ the open subscheme $\{y\}$ of $X_s$ is isomorphic over $\kappa(s)$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], where the residue field $\kappa(y)$ is a finite field extension of $\kappa(s)$ every element of which is a root of a separable polynomial over $\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-separable-polynomial].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), part (2), line 8175; its proof: part (1) via Algebra, Lemma 00U3 (algebra-lemma-etale-over-field) and Morphisms, Lemma 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre); the fibre is etale over kappa(s) by Morphisms, Lemma 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale)
